resolutions.researcher_notes: All three original refs (africanenergycouncil.org, pipeline-journal.net, agcnewsnet.com) are dead/unreachable; did not need Wayback since multiple live independent sources were found. Replaced with 4 working, mutually independent sources confirming the 'proposed' status: (1) leadership.ng (Nigerian daily, LEADERSHIP News) — reports the Sept 2024 GASTECH Houston meeting between Nigeria's Petroleum Minister (Gas) Ekperikpe Ekpo and Libya's Oil Minister Khalifa Abdel Sadeg, citing the 5,600km figure and 13-nation route, matching the brief's value. (2) libyaherald.com (Libya Herald, bylined Sami Zaptia, editor-in-chief) — independently reports the same Sept 2024 meeting and the agreement to prepare an MoU on feasibility studies for a Nigeria-to-Europe pipeline via Libya; does not cite the 5,600km figure itself but corroborates the proposal/talks. (3) libyareview.com (Libya Review) — separate Libyan outlet, confirms the Nigeria-Libya pipeline discussion (via Niger/Chad to Europe) though its 5,600km reference is to the competing Nigeria-Morocco/NIGAL route, not this one; cited for corroboration of the talks themselves, not the distance figure. (4) ecofinagency.com (Ecofin Agency, pan-African financial/trade press, bylined Abdel-Latif Boureima) — a later, distinct story (Sept 2025) reporting 'revived' Nigeria-Libya pipeline talks, feasibility studies, and a planned MoU, citing a somewhat different route length (~3,300km) than the brief's 5,600km — treated as corroborating the underlying proposal/talks (status = proposed), not the specific distance. Status 'proposed' is confirmed by inference across all four: feasibility studies, technical exchanges, and a planned-but-unsigned MoU, with no construction or FID reported anywhere. Sources span three outlets/countries (Nigeria, Libya x2, pan-African wire) and two distinct reporting cycles (2024, 2025) — genuinely independent, not the same wire story republished.
